Eleven point three seconds.
That is how long my users stared at a white screen before the most important element on my dashboard appeared.
I did not know. My localhost loaded in under a second. Chrome DevTools on my M2 MacBook showed no problems. Everything felt fast, because everything was fast on my machine.
Then I ran Lighthouse with simulated throttling on a mid-range phone. 11.3 seconds. The number hit me the way a production bug hits at 2 AM, except this one had been live for six months.
LCP, Largest Contentful Paint, is the single metric that decides whether your user sees your app or your competitor’s. Google uses it for search rankings. Users use it to decide if your app is broken. And Angular apps fail it more often than any framework should, for reasons that are entirely fixable.
Here are the 8 fixes I applied, the before-and-after LCP for each, and the order that matters. Your LCP is probably not 11.3 seconds. But I would bet money it is above 2.5.
What LCP Actually Measures (And Why Angular Apps Fail It)
